is_anopheles.evidence: The paper studies Anopheles gambiae (page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports the Vgsc L995S (1014S) mutation (page 5, section 2.2: 'all mosquitoes that we sequenced (n = 9) harbored the resistance allele (1014S)').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper states that all 9 sequenced mosquitoes were homozygous for the 1014S allele (page 5, section 2.2).

african_field_population.evidence: The mosquitoes were collected from highland areas around the Kisumu district in western Kenya (page 2, section 2.1; page 6, section 4.1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study involving sequencing of field-collected mosquitoes (page 1, Abstract).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies 'highland areas around the Kisumu district' in Kenya (page 2, section 2.1; page 6, section 4.1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The paper was received in 2014 and accepted in 2015, and the study describes recent collections (page 1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new sequencing project of 9 wild-caught mosquitoes.

supplement.evidence: The required data (genotype of the 9 mosquitoes) is provided in the main text.

assessment.summary: This study sequenced the genomes of 9 wild-caught Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes from the Kisumu district, Kenya, to construct a genome-wide LD map. It identified the Vgsc L995S (1014S) mutation in all 9 sequenced individuals.
